plan_a_advantages: Includes threshold and hill workouts for power and climbing strength.
Incorporates strength training to support durability and injury prevention.
Offers a more varied training stimulus to target different aspects of trail running.
plan_b_advantages: Prioritizes recovery, which is essential for any training plan.
Features a longer, moderate-paced trail run, providing valuable time on the trails.
Provides a more consistent, low-impact training schedule.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it incorporates targeted workouts designed to improve specific aspects of trail running performance. While Plan B focuses heavily on recovery and easy runs, which is important, it lacks the structured intensity needed for speed development. Plan A includes a threshold run, hill sessions, and strength work, all crucial for building the physiological adaptations required for faster times on trails. Plan B’s emphasis on recovery, while beneficial, risks hindering progress towards the athlete’s goal of increased speed.
